## Design of the experiment

This experiment is analogous to the experiment with a normal data generating mechanism. 
In that experiment, we assumed the use of **split-samples**: on a certain location a single field protocol (support area, number of sub-samples, depth) would be used to collect a single compound sample based on a mixture of sub-samples, and this compound sample would be split in half and that each half would be analysed with two different lab methods. 
However, this interpretation of double-sampling is at odds with the interpretation in SoilHarmony.
In this experiment we therefore simulate the data according to this revised interpretation; namely that on a certain location, two different field protocols are used to collect two different compound samples and each compound sample is analysed with a different lab method. 
A TF derived on such paired data can only be used to map a unique pair of (field protocol, lab method) to a pair of (reference field protocol, reference lab method) as the field and lab components cannot be disentangled from such data.

We make use of the following new notation and relations:

- point values of the soil descriptor - values at point locations the size of the sampling equipment, eg. 1 cm² - have a variance in the population (area $A$) of $\sigma^2(p, A)$
- the variance of the support-area average per location in the population, $\sigma^2(a, A)$, decreases with size of the support-area: as $a$ -> $A$, $\sigma^2(a, A)$ -> 0
- the variance of the point values within a location, $\sigma^2(p, a)$, increases with size of the support-area of the location: as $a$ -> $A$, $\sigma^2(p, a)$ -> $\sigma^2(p, A)$
- Krige's relation says the total remains constant: $\sigma^2(p, A) = \sigma^2(a, A) + \sigma^2(p, a)$
- assuming that variance of the average per location is proportional to area: $\sigma^2(a, A) \propto a^{-\alpha}$ ($\alpha$ = scaling exponent (0 < $\alpha$ < 1 defines spatial autocorrelation), we can see that the variances of the average per location are related to each other:
$\sigma^2(a_2, A) = \sigma^2(a_1, A) \left(\frac{a_1}{a_2}\right)^{\alpha}$

The above allow us to simulate paired data as follows. 

We start with simulating $N$ paired values of the latent support-area averages for each field protocol [(1) & (2)] as measured with the non-reference method $X$:
$$
\begin{pmatrix} X_{\mathrm{latent}}^{(1)}\\ X_{\mathrm{latent}}^{(2)} \end{pmatrix} 
\sim \mathcal{N}
\left(
\begin{pmatrix} \mu_X \\ \mu_X \end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix} \sigma^2(a_1, A)\ & \rho\sigma(a_1, A)\sigma(a_2, A) \\ 
\rho\sigma(a_1, A)\sigma(a_2, A) & \sigma^2(a_2, A) \end{pmatrix}
\right)
$$
, i.e. we simulate latent values for the non-reference method under both field protocols. Later on we will just retain only one value from this and ignore the other.

Next we transform the latent non-reference method to the reference method under both field protocols. Same as above, later on we will just retain only one value from this and ignore the other.

$$
\begin{aligned}
Y_{\mathrm{latent}}^{(1)} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1X_{\mathrm{latent}}^{(1)} \\
Y_{\mathrm{latent}}^{(2)} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1X_{\mathrm{latent}}^{(2)}
\end{aligned}
$$

We add now simulated field measurement error. 
The field measurement error comes from approximating support-area averages with $n$ sub-samples and follows the usual variance of the mean formula: $\frac{\sigma^2(p, a)}{n}$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\begin{pmatrix} \epsilon^{(1)}\\ \epsilon^{(2)} \end{pmatrix} 
&\sim \mathcal{N}
\left(
\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix} \frac{\sigma^2(p, a_1)}{n_1}\ & \rho_f\frac{\sigma(p, a_1)\sigma(p, a_2)}{\sqrt{n_1n_2}} \\ 
\rho_f\frac{\sigma(p, a_1)\sigma(p, a_2)}{\sqrt{n_1n_2}} & \frac{\sigma^2(p, a_2)}{n_2} \end{pmatrix}
\right) \\
X_{\mathrm{obs,field}}^{(1)} &= X_{\mathrm{latent}}^{(1)} + \epsilon^{(1)}  \\
Y_{\mathrm{obs,field}}^{(1)} &= Y_{\mathrm{latent}}^{(1)} + \epsilon^{(1)}  \\
X_{\mathrm{obs,field}}^{(2)} &= X_{\mathrm{latent}}^{(2)} + \epsilon^{(2)}  \\
Y_{\mathrm{obs,field}}^{(2)} &= Y_{\mathrm{latent}}^{(2)} + \epsilon^{(2)} 
\end{aligned}
$$
(in all generality, we allow measurement error between both field protocols to be correlated with magnitude $\rho_f$ but we expect this value to be low; correlation could occur when point locations would overlap exactly between two field protocols)



The following values of each parameter are examined. One parameter is varied at a time while the others are kept at the default value (first value indicated). This gives a total of `r length(unique(prediction$scenario_label))` scenario's: each scenario is replicated `r nrep` times.
The values are chosen to approximate realistic values for pH.

| Parameter                                        | Values                |
|--------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|
|$N$                                               |200, 100, 500          |
|$\mu$                                             |7                      |
|$\sigma^2(p,A)$                                   |2                      |
|$\sigma^2(a_1,A)$                                 |1.9                    |
|$a_1 / a2$                                        |1, 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, 1.3  |
|$n_1$                                             |5, 2, 10, 20           |
|$n_1 / n_2$                                       |1, 0.8, 1.2            |
|$\alpa$                                           |0.1, 0.05, 0.2         |
|$\rho_{\text{latent}}$                            |0.9, 0.99              |
|$\rho_{\text{me, field}}$                         |0                      |
|$\rho_{\text{me, lab}}$                           |0                      |
|$\beta_0$                                         |0, 0.1, 0.2            |
|$\beta_1$                                         |1, 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, 1.3  |
|$\sigma_{\text{lab}}(X) / \sigma_{\text{field}}$  |0.05, 0.01, 0.1, 0.2   |
|$\sigma_{\text{lab}}(Y) / \sigma_{\text{lab}}(X)$ |1                      |

: Table: Parameter values for the scenario's. The default value is the first in each list.

## Description of the models

Simple linear regression (frequentist).

<br>

## Evaluation of the models

See report normal DGM: R², PICP, MAE, MPE, RMSE, SDPE

<br>

## Results


```{r, echo=F}
# point-estimate (prediction interval) metrics
display_results <- function(paramname) {
  prediction %>% 
    filter(grepl(paramname, scenario_label)) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      c(PICP, MAE, MPE, RMSE, R2, SDPE), 
      names_to = "metric", values_to = "value"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      metric = factor(metric, c("MPE","MAE","RMSE","R2","SDPE","PICP"),
                      c("MPE","MAE","RMSE","R²","SDPE","PICP")),
      scenario_value = stringr::str_extract(
        scenario_label, "-?\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?"
      )
    ) %>%
    ggplot(aes(factor(scenario_value), value)) +
    facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
    geom_boxplot() +
    geom_jitter(height = 0, alpha = .2) +
    labs(x = "", y = "") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
          legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

```{r, echo=F}
#| label: fig-samplesize
#| fig-cap: "Sample size of the calibration (training) dataset"
display_results("Nsample") +
  labs(x = "sample size")
```

```{r, echo=F}
#| label: fig-ratioarea
#| fig-cap: "Ratio between the support area's of both field protocols"
display_results("RatioArea") +
  labs(x = "a1 / a2")
```

```{r, echo=F}
#| label: fig-ratioarea
#| fig-cap: "Ratio between the support area's of both field protocols"
display_results("RatioArea") +
  labs(x = "a1 / a2")
```

```{r, echo=F}
#| label: fig-nsubsamples
#| fig-cap: "Number of subsamples"
display_results("Nsubsamples") +
  labs(x = "n")
```

```{r, echo=F}
#| label: fig-ratiosubsamples
#| fig-cap: "Ratio between subsamples in both protocols"
display_results("RatioSubsamples") +
  labs(x = "n1 / n2")
```

```{r, echo=F}
#| label: fig-spatautocor
#| fig-cap: "Spatial autocorrelation (zero = absolute smoothness)"
display_results("SpatAutocor") +
  labs(x = "alpha")
```

```{r, echo=F}
#| label: fig-corrlatent
#| fig-cap: "Correlation between latent support-area averages"
display_results("CorrLatent") +
  labs(x = "rho(latent)")
```

```{r, echo=F}
#| label: fig-beta0
#| fig-cap: "Intercept of the TF between the latent support-area averages"
display_results("Intercept") +
  labs(x = "beta0")
```

```{r, echo=F}
#| label: fig-beta1
#| fig-cap: "Slope of the TF between the latent support-area averages"
display_results("Slope") +
  labs(x = "beta1")
```

```{r, echo=F}
#| label: fig-ratiolabfield
#| fig-cap: "Ratio between measurement error: lab / field"
display_results("RatioLabField") +
  labs(x = "sigma(lab) / sigma(field)")
```

<br>

## Conclusions

- the derived TF's in this way are valid only for a mapping of 1 pair of (field protocol, lab method) to another pair and cannot be used in any other way; this probably means that only national TF's can be developed as all countries have slight variations in field protocols
- coverage is preserved
- EIV-models would need even more parameters as before (see other experiments), making it even more un-identifiable probably
